svg.title: Laterna — application map

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: Version 10.65.1 · 2026-11-19 · one page, eight zones, from the widest view to the finest
Every box names the file, route or function that carries it, so the map doubles as an index into the code. Reasons live in DOC-TECH.md, DECISIONS.md and CLAUDE.md.

Vector drawing: zoom freely. Self-hosted media front end with its own in-browser player (Lumen) — Next.js, React, TypeScript, SQLite — over Jellyfin, Radarr, Sonarr, Jellyseerr, qBittorrent, Bazarr, Jackett.

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: Everything a viewer sees goes through src/proxy.ts; nothing in the browser talks to an upstream service directly. Three callers come in without a session cookie: a television (a signed pass for one title's stream and subtitles), a Stream Deck (its own bearer token), and the server itself warming its catalogue routes over loopback. Configuration and secrets live in data/ beside the database (DECISIONS §48), so a fresh install needs no .env. A copy of the application started with CINE_BACKGROUND_JOBS=off

(backgroundJobs.ts) runs none of the timers, only the read-only catalogue warm-ups (§145). A route never writes Content-Encoding or Content-Length itself: it sets x-cine-encoding / x-cine-length, and boot.mjs turns them into the real headers (§131).

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: what the box names is where it lives in the code
database, log file, browser storage, cache
each outgoing arrow is labelled with its answer
a place (browser, container) or a family of files
solid: happens on the normal path
dotted: a push, a fallback, a background task, a hint
the label says what travels, or when
solid arrow: a call · dashed: its answer
Start at zone 1 for the whole system, then follow a viewer: the interfaces (2), the player
— its native path, its safety net and casting (3), one playback end to end (4), what is
cached where (5), what is written down (6), what the gate lets through (7), and the
optional features (8). Boxes named « section 3 » or « 3b » refer to zone 3.

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: Three roles: admin, user, and share for a share link (DECISIONS §112). Hiding the administration group and the management link is presentation only: a user who types /gestion is sent back to /, and the management reads answer 403 (ADMIN_ONLY_PAGES, ADMIN_ONLY_READS, diagram 7). Every cinema screen is a field of the address hash, so Back steps out one screen at a time; desktop and phone are two layouts sharing one function per decision (DECISIONS §31, §52, §74, §81, The sheet lifecycle in CLAUDE.md).

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: 3 · The player — src/lib/webcodecs/ and the hosts around it

No pixel and no copied audio sample passes through JavaScript: the remuxer only rewrites the packaging. Sound that cannot cross MediaSource is read by the player's own packet reader, decoded in the tab and encoded again; no third-party media library is involved since 19/11/2026 (§197), and any audio error hands the film to

the server player rather than playing it silent. A refusal is always a named string, which the activity page groups by. Every file plays through this path on every engine: the server-side remux that served Safari as HLS (Lumen serveur) is archived, and every old /api/lumen/* address answers 410 (§196).
3a · Choosing a path, and the native pipeline

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: The server player is a safety net, not a second product: it plays what the native path refuses, what a slow link cannot carry and what goes to a television. Jellyfin decides between DirectPlay, DirectStream and Transcode; every byte still goes through the application's relay. A

MediaSource stream cannot leave the tab, so a television always gets Jellyfin's stream through the server player; the page becomes a remote control (Chromecast) or hands its element's route over (AirPlay). The server keeps the resume point when the page goes quiet. A Chromecast

that accepts the load and shows no picture within 25 s is relaunched once with its sound re-encoded to AAC stereo, then the failure is said — the Cast kit names no receiver's decoders (CAST_NO_PICTURE_MS, DECISIONS §122).
3b · The server player and the slow connection

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: One session id joins every line of a playback; a rebuild rewrites start under the same id. A page killed by iOS sends its summary at the next launch (why: "lost"), and a position Jellyfin never received leaves through unsentPosition. The

start line is also what orders an actors-on-screen analysis — the only line all three players send, with the item and the position. resumeAt: 0 means from the beginning; an absent resumeAt means ask the server.

[refusal, audio error, slow link or cast]

svg.text: mount — PlayerHost picks the native player
GET stream, Range — header and index, OPFS first
probePlaybackPath → RemuxPlayback → init and first segments
POST /api/player/log — opening, start (session, build, openedFrom, resumeFrom)
order the item (high), the next episode (normal)
HostSeek — refill from the keyframe before the target
rebuild the pipeline at the same position
fallToStable — fallback line, server player continues, 3b
stop — marks watched past the threshold
stop line — watched, waits, seeks, diag.*, timeline
keepOnStop — keep the restart passage in OPFS
refreshAfterPlayback — after the stop report and once the screen is free
revalidate resume, next-up, progress, series episodes, lists

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: The cinema opens on what the device kept, then the network corrects it; the catalogue is frozen on purpose (it changes daily), only the resume and next-up feeds follow focus, and the two catalogues are re-read on a return to the foreground once fifteen minutes old. While a film fills the screen SWR is paused, which is why the player's own queries carry

playerBootstrapOptions and why closing the player revalidates explicitly. The network's own answers lean on the browser's HTTP cache — the catalogue's ETag (a 304 when nothing changed), images immutable for a year — and on WebKit that cache is only read back across launches when the service worker answers the request: it relays images and the two catalogues +

Nouveautés itself there (RELAY_THROUGH_WORKER, public/sw.js); a request it lets fall through was downloaded in full at every iPhone launch. The banner's logos and poster go through the image optimiser as WebP (bannerImage).

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: Player line kinds (PlayerEventKind): opening, start, fallback, network, rebuild, error, seek, stall, audio, pause, cast, reserve, subtitle-gen, fluidite, debut-scene, stop. Every
native and server line carries session and build; incident lines carry timeline, and stall/stop carry diag.*. Offline downloads write one line per step (requested, started, ready,
failed, fetched, cancelled, removed, expired, deleted) to server.log under scope: "offline", beside scope: "download" for the original file; the Activity panel reads them there.
Bench and dev lines never reach player.log, so they never count as a viewer's. recherche.log and the AI lines never hold the sentence typed, the question or the answer.

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: The interface never enforces a permission: src/proxy.ts refuses whatever a user should not do, and sends every share session to shareGate, where anything not listed does not exist. Without a session cookie only a television (one title, its stream and subtitles), the server's own loopback warm-up and the routes that carry their own check (Stream Deck token, share password, address-move code) get through.

g.font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: Each of these is off, or reaches nothing, until an administrator configures it, and none of them changes how a film plays. Actors on screen (DECISIONS §138, §141, §143, §151, src/lib/xray/) are computed by a separate service, laterna-xray, with its own image and its own SQLite: it decodes each file with ffmpeg, recognises faces against TMDB photos and names voices from those faces. Laterna orders an analysis when a playback starts and from a background scheduler, and the player reads the scenes once per item. The same service measures subtitle sync on request; nothing is written to a media or subtitle file. The

service, its API contract and its measurements: xray/README.md. AI features (§135, §137, §139, §140) share the generated subtitles' provider, key and monthly ceiling; their sources are built on the server from what the account has watched only, and every answer passes the same name check before it is shown. Books (§127–§129) are a mode of the cinema (livres=1 in the hash), never a third tab, and the reader runs in a same-origin frame so closing a book reloads nothing. Library cleanup (§198) is the one place that deletes titles: a full removal goes through qBittorrent, Radarr/Sonarr, Jellyseerr and Jellyfin, since

the library's files are hard links of what qBittorrent shares and the media mount is read-only here. Share links (§112) open one film or one series with a password until an end date; the Stream Deck (§120) reads the plays in progress and their posters, nothing else.
